card.name: Kuchipudi
card.era: Roots in Natya Shastra; 10th-c inscriptions; systematized 17th c
card.tagline: Andhra Pradesh's classical dance-drama danced on a brass plate
card.profile: Kuchipudi is one of the eight major Indian classical dance forms, originating in the village of Kuchipudi in the Krishna district of Andhra Pradesh (Wikipedia). A dance-drama rooted in the Natya Shastra and the Vaishnavism tradition centered on Krishna, it blends fast rhythmic footwork, sculpturesque poses, expressive eyes and dramatic narrative, performed to Carnatic music (Wikipedia). A signature element is the tarangam, in which the dancer performs on the rim of a brass plate. Evidence of an older form appears in 10th-century copper inscriptions and the 15th-century Machupalli Kaifat (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Historically performed by male Brahmin troupes (Bhagavatulu) and traditionally credited with refinement by the saint Siddhendra Yogi, Kuchipudi is recognized among the classical dance forms by the Sangeet Natak Akademi (Cultural India).
